Subject: Re: production spike - streaming errors and timeout patterns

Hi Vivek,

We started seeing a sharp increase in error rate on our production ingestion pipeline starting 15:42 PDT. Approximately 9% of streams are failing with a parser error and several sessions dropped with timeout. Attached is a small snippet of the error log and a short pcap we captured on our side.

Key details:
- Client: Acme event forwarder v2.1.3 (your JS SDK)
- Error seen: downstream parser reports malformed metadata frames leading to de-serialization failure
- Impact: backlog of ~120 events per minute, retries adding noticeable latency to downstream workers
- Reproducible: yes, our ops team can reproduce by sending multi-part messages with a specific header ordering

We need an urgent triage. Can you escalate to engineering? This is affecting our customer checkout funnel.

Thanks,
Sarah

Subject: URGENT: ACME - metadata fragmentation causing request failures

Lauren, Markus,

Looping you both in. Acme has a reproducible production spike tied to our client SDK (v2.1.3). They report malformed metadata frames hitting the streaming parser and resulting in de-serialization failures and timeouts. They attached logs and a pcap.

Impact: checkout latency and lost events, they estimate 9% error rate on affected streams. This is an active revenue-impacting outage for a top-tier customer. They can reproduce and believe specific header ordering causes frame fragmentation.

What we need now:
- Immediate triage from SDK/runtime team to confirm whether this is an SDK encoding bug or a parser robustness issue in the runtime.
- If SDK bug, provide mitigation steps and a temporary fallback we can push as a patch or recommend to the customer.
- Exec-level summary + ETA to share with Acme leadership.

I started a private Slack channel with Acme, and I can share the pcap in that channel if needed.

Vivek
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Acme Platform Ops <platform-ops@acme-corp.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Apr 2027 17:02:00 -0700
Subject: RE: URGENT: ACME - metadata fragmentation causing request failures

Thanks Vivek,

Initial triage notes from runtime/SDK triage:
- We reproduced a similar de-serialization error locally using the provided pcap. The failure mode occurs when multi-part headers are split across TCP frames and our client-side encoder emits a metadata header chunk boundary that the runtime parser currently treats as a hard delimiter.
- Hypothesis: a combination of our encoder emitting optional metadata fields and an HTTP/2 frame split on the client produces an out-of-order header sequence; the streaming parser assumes contiguous header frames and fails when it receives an unexpected continuation token.

Short term mitigations we can offer to Acme:
1) Ask Acme to flip client-side feature flag to disable optional header shuffling (available in v2.1.3 via environment variable REDWOOD_METADATA_ORDER=stable). This is low risk and avoids full rollback.
2) Push a hotfix to the runtime that relaxes strict continuation handling for header frames; estimated patch ready in 24-36 hours, testing included.
3) Provide a diagnostic-enabled SDK build for Acme to validate ordering changes (non-production).

Attached internal trace: we added more defensive checks around continuation tokens and the parser recovers without dropping frames in our test harness.

Lauren Bishop
Engineering Manager, Runtime

Thanks for the quick follow-up. We validated the REDWOOD_METADATA_ORDER=stable flag in our staging and the error rate dropped to under 0.5% during a 45-minute run.

We can flip the flag in prod as a temporary measure but would prefer a runtime fix so we can keep optional metadata fields and our current client implementation. Please share the hotfix ETA and any rollback instructions in case of regressions.

Also attaching a small trace from our staging run which shows the reduced failure frequency when ordering is stable.

-Rajesh

Thanks team. Quick notes for execs and next steps:

- Summary: Client SDK v2.1.3 can emit optional metadata in an order that, when combined with TCP/HTTP2 frame splitting, leads to fragmented header frames that our streaming parser treats as fatal. Customer impact: increased error rate and latency on critical flows.
- Short term: advise Acme to flip REDWOOD_METADATA_ORDER=stable (they validated this reduces errors).
- Mid term: runtime hotfix to relax continuation handling; Lauren estimates 24-36 hours for patch + 12 hours testing and can provide a staged rollout plan.
- Owner: Lauren and runtime team to deliver patch. Vivek to coordinate customer communication and verify rollback plan.

Please confirm:
1) ETA for a runtime build we can release to Acme for verification? (Lauren)
2) Recommended customer-facing wording for the communications we send after the patch is live? (Vivek)
